title: A new example changes a familiar rule

captions.physics: Giving a thought a visible expression
captions.emotions: Trusting a meaning you both understand

meaning: A concrete example can renew your shared view when an important realisation brings genuine meaning to a familiar principle.
text: Familiar words sometimes gain meaning only after a discovery of your own. The Empress in the physical position of Ajna suggests creating examples and giving the thought under discussion a visible form. Judgement in energy supports responding to a significant realisation and reconsidering an earlier explanation. The Hierophant in emotions feels supported by a shared meaning, the pleasure of understanding a principle you trust. A familiar formulation can feel closer once you see a concrete connection behind it and explain it in your own words.

For example, you prepare a short account of a journey together and try removing several details. Suddenly “keep what matters” means preserving the story’s central theme. **Your own realisation gives substance to a familiar rule.** Cutting previously looked like losing interesting scenes; now you can see which connection needs to remain. A clear principle becomes a satisfying foundation for discussing the account. The example shows why some details contribute to its meaning while others are unnecessary.

The difficulty is citing the principle after your discovery before the other person has seen the same connection. Understandable words can become a ready answer again. Your wish to respond to fresh meaning retains its value when each person has room for a discovery of their own. A shared direction becomes truly mutual through an understandable example as well as agreement with a successful formulation.
